hardware.execution: Go API, generator and SDK share one Windows process; native Centrifugo on same host; PostgreSQL 18.6 Docker Linux tmpfs

adopted.reply_reads: One pgx batch containing separate lock and full retry-result statements, fresh READ COMMITTED snapshot after waiting; reference lookup selects only ID and root ownership
adopted.admission: Restored exact 0.4.3 admission source: 2 active and 12 active/waiting per counter, 12 global active writes for pool 16, 256 total active/waiting, 2s shared wait. Preliminary borrowing and dynamic-share policies were tested and rejected, not retained in production
adopted.metrics: Successful and capacity-refused latency distributions separate; existing all-attempt and arrival accounting preserved

notes: Same 4/16 hot topic and 512/1024 actual WSS subscriber workload in every run, fixed arrival rates, 3s warmup, 12s measured launch windows, no retries.

One current baseline, one SQL-only candidate, two preliminary borrowing candidates and two rejected dynamic-share repetitions and one final SQL-only verification and an ending repeat of the same frozen baseline; all source variants and worse outcomes retained. This is a stepwise comparison, not a randomized factorial experiment.
The same baseline binary was repeated at the end because final throughput fell; before/after drift is retained and no stable percentage speedup is claimed.
No new runtime dependency, migration, table sharding or change to product authorization rules. Benchmarks still use threaded posts, root/child/root-quote/child-quote cases.

Rejected share candidate used currently live counters, not product quotas; sustained-load regressions were observed; one scheduled ordinary write remained unsent in the second dynamic-share trial, and later baseline drift prevents attributing every regression to the policy. Final production admission was restored byte-for-byte; none of these candidate policies is claimed adopted.

Longer queues absorb bursts but do not increase service capacity. Unsent client demand and HTTP 503 remain explicit. Success-only latency and receiver latency must not be compared with refusal-dominated all-attempt percentiles.
Per-request SQL statement count stays 8 without a reference, 9 with one; the first two queries are now one driver batch. Driver call counts are not physical packet counts.

Every phase verifies request to database author/body/root/quote/continuous position and canonical payload/event identity at every receiver, then bounded outbox drain. Expected fanout uses actual commits, never offered or refused requests.
Client/server CPU and random stream UUID partition collisions remain uncontrolled. Disk/network/slow readers/reconnect storms/credential refresh/soak and 30,000 concurrent users remain unaccepted.

One full-suite process exited status 1 without an assertion or stack trace. Same-source verbose full regression passed subsequently; original incomplete log retained. Root cause of that process exit is unconfirmed, not claimed fixed.
Only synthetic aggregate results and source fingerprints are shared; UUID literals in EXPLAIN are redacted. Private runtime retains raw outputs and frozen binaries.
